text: What is the correct first step in the standard troubleshooting methodology?

options.text: Identify the problem by gathering information from the user and system

text: After establishing a theory of probable cause, what should a technician do next?

options.text: Test the theory to determine the actual cause
Reinstall the operating system regardless of the issue

text: Why is documenting findings, actions, and outcomes an important final step in troubleshooting?

options.text: It is legally required in every country
It creates a record that helps with future troubleshooting and knowledge sharing
It is optional and rarely useful
It replaces the need to verify the fix worked

text: What component is often called the 'brain' of the computer, executing instructions?
What happens to the data stored in RAM when a computer is powered off?

options.text: It is lost, since RAM is volatile memory
It is automatically backed up to the CPU
It moves to the power supply

text: Which storage type has no moving parts and is generally faster and more durable than a traditional hard drive?
What is the main circuit board that connects and allows communication between a computer's core components?
What is the function of a computer's power supply unit (PSU)?

options.text: To convert AC power from the wall outlet into DC power the components can use

text: Which Windows file system is most commonly used on modern internal hard drives, supporting large file sizes and permissions?
Which file system is commonly recommended for USB flash drives that need to work across Windows, macOS, and Linux with large file support?
What is a key limitation of the FAT32 file system?

options.text: It cannot be used on USB drives
It has a maximum individual file size of 4 GB
It cannot be read by any operating system

text: Which connector type is most commonly used today for connecting keyboards, mice, and external storage?
Which video connector type is a digital standard that also carries audio, commonly used for TVs and monitors?
What type of connector is used for standard wired Ethernet network connections?
What type of connector is typically used for telephone/landline connections?
VGA is what type of video signal?
What should a technician do first before opening a desktop computer case to work inside it?

options.text: Power off the system and unplug it from the wall outlet
Remove the RAM first while it's still powered on

text: What is the purpose of an anti-static (ESD) wrist strap when working inside a computer?

options.text: To prevent electrostatic discharge from damaging sensitive electronic components
To measure voltage output of the PSU

text: A user reports their computer won't power on at all - no lights, no fans. What is a reasonable first thing to check?

options.text: Whether the power cable is properly plugged in and the outlet/power strip is working

text: A Windows PC repeatedly crashes with a 'Blue Screen of Death' (BSOD). What does this generally indicate?

options.text: The user's account password has expired
A serious system-level error, often related to drivers, hardware, or memory
The monitor brightness is too low

text: A computer is running very slowly and Task Manager shows very high disk usage with normal CPU usage. What is a reasonable next troubleshooting step?

options.text: Check for malware, disk errors, or excessive background processes/services using the disk
Assume it is a network cabling issue

text: A user's printer shows as offline. What is a common, simple first troubleshooting step?

options.text: Check that the printer is powered on and properly connected (USB/network) before deeper diagnosis

text: What is the general difference between an inkjet printer and a laser printer?

options.text: Inkjet printers use liquid ink sprayed onto paper; laser printers use toner fused to paper with heat
Laser printers use liquid ink; inkjet printers use toner
Laser printers cannot print in color

text: What short-range wireless technology is commonly used to connect devices like wireless headphones or a mouse over short distances?
What wireless technology enables contactless payments and quick pairing by tapping devices close together?
What is 'active listening' in the context of customer service for IT support?

options.text: Multitasking on other tickets while a user explains their issue
Fully concentrating on, understanding, and responding thoughtfully to what the user is saying
Interrupting the user to speed up the call
Only listening to the first sentence of a complaint

text: What is the purpose of a ticketing system in an IT support environment?

options.text: To track, prioritize, and document support requests from creation to resolution
To replace the need for any troubleshooting

text: What does an SLA (Service Level Agreement) typically define in a support context?

options.text: The exact brand of hardware a company must use
Expected response and resolution times for support requests
The programming language used by developers

text: When should a helpdesk technician escalate a ticket to a higher tier of support?

options.text: Never - all issues must be resolved at the first tier
When the issue is beyond their expertise, access level, or requires specialized tools
Immediately for every single ticket regardless of difficulty
Only if the user asks for a manager

text: What is the benefit of performing regular preventive maintenance on computers (e.g. cleaning dust, updating software)?

options.text: It guarantees hardware will never fail
It reduces the likelihood of failures and extends the useful life of equipment
It voids the manufacturer's warranty in all cases

text: Which Windows command-line tool is used to check and repair file system errors on a drive?
Which Windows command-line tool lists currently running processes?
Which Windows command-line utility scans and repairs corrupted or missing system files?
On Linux, which command lists the contents of the current directory?
On Linux, which command is used to change the current working directory?
On Linux, which command displays the current working directory's full path?
What is the general purpose of Safe Mode when booting Windows?

options.text: To boot with a minimal set of drivers and services for troubleshooting purposes
To permanently disable the operating system
To speed up normal daily use

text: What is a common first step when a laptop won't connect to Wi-Fi but other devices on the same network work fine?

options.text: Confirm Wi-Fi is enabled on the laptop (not in airplane mode) and try reconnecting/restarting networking
Reset the entire office router immediately without further checks
Assume it's an ISP outage without checking other devices

text: What generally happens to files when they are deleted and then removed from the Recycle Bin/Trash?

options.text: They are instantly and permanently unrecoverable by any method
The space is marked as available for reuse, but the data may still be recoverable until overwritten
They are automatically emailed to the user
They are moved to a second hard drive automatically

text: Why should you avoid opening unknown email attachments from unfamiliar senders?

options.text: They always use too much storage space
They may contain malware that can compromise the system
They will automatically slow down the email server only
There is no real risk if antivirus is installed

text: What is the general purpose of a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) for computer equipment?

options.text: To permanently increase a computer's processing speed
To provide short-term backup power and protect against power surges during outages
To replace the need for a power supply unit

text: A user says their mobile phone screen isn't responding to touch. What is a reasonable basic first step?

options.text: Restart the device and check if a screen protector or debris is interfering with touch input
Reformat the phone's storage without saving data

text: What does 'remote desktop support' allow a technician to do?

options.text: Physically travel faster to a user's location
View and control a user's computer screen remotely to diagnose and fix issues
Print documents from anywhere in the world

text: Why is it good practice to confirm a fix with the end user before closing a support ticket?

options.text: It isn't necessary if the technician is confident
To verify from the user's perspective that the original issue is actually resolved
It is only needed for hardware issues, never software
Tickets should never be closed once opened

text: What is a reasonable way to communicate a technical issue to a non-technical user?

options.text: Use as much technical jargon as possible to sound credible
Explain the issue and solution in clear, plain language appropriate to their level of understanding
Avoid explaining anything and just fix it silently
Tell them it's too complicated to explain

text: What generally distinguishes a laptop's battery health issue from a charging port issue?

options.text: There's no way to distinguish them
A battery issue often shows poor holding of charge even when plugged in works fine; a port issue often means it won't charge at all even when plugged in
Battery issues only happen on desktops

text: What is the purpose of Device Manager in Windows?

options.text: To view and manage hardware devices and their drivers
To manage installed printer ink levels only

text: What does it usually mean when Device Manager shows a yellow exclamation mark next to a device?

options.text: There is a driver or hardware problem with that device
The device has been permanently disabled by the manufacturer
The device is using too much RAM

text: What is the general purpose of System Restore in Windows?

options.text: To permanently delete all user files
To revert system files and settings to a previous point in time without affecting personal files
To reinstall Windows from scratch every time

text: Why is it important to keep operating systems and software patched/updated?

options.text: Updates serve no real purpose besides cosmetic changes
Updates often fix security vulnerabilities and bugs
Updates always make computers run slower with no benefit
They are only needed once, at the time of purchase

text: A user reports 'no internet' but can access some websites and not others. What does this suggest?

options.text: A total loss of internet connectivity
The connection likely works, but there may be a DNS issue or the specific sites/services are down
The computer's power supply has failed
The keyboard needs to be replaced

text: What is the purpose of Windows' 'Event Viewer'?

options.text: To review logs of system, application, and security events for troubleshooting

text: What is a common cause of a computer's clock/date resetting incorrectly every time it's powered off?

options.text: A dying or dead CMOS battery on the motherboard

text: What should you generally check first if a desktop monitor shows no signal at all?

options.text: That the video cable is securely connected at both the monitor and the computer, and the monitor is powered on

text: What is the benefit of using a knowledge base or documented solutions when resolving support tickets?

options.text: It helps technicians resolve known issues faster and maintain consistency
It replaces the need to talk to the user at all
It is only useful for hardware issues

text: What is 'onboarding' in an IT support context, such as for a new employee?

options.text: Removing a departing employee's access permanently
Setting up accounts, hardware, and access for a new employee
Installing malware protection only on servers

text: Why is it good practice to remove a departing employee's system access promptly ('offboarding')?

options.text: To reduce the security risk of former employees retaining access to company systems and data
It is only relevant for physical office keys, not IT systems
It should be delayed as long as possible

text: What is a reasonable approach when a user is frustrated or upset about a recurring IT issue?

options.text: Argue with the user about whose fault it is
Stay calm, acknowledge their frustration, and focus on resolving the issue professionally
Hang up or end the chat immediately
Ignore their concerns and move to the next ticket

text: What is the purpose of asking clarifying questions when a user submits a vague support request?

options.text: To delay helping them as long as possible
To accurately understand the actual problem before attempting a fix
It is unnecessary; technicians should always guess
To make the user feel unwelcome

text: What is the main risk of plugging an unknown USB drive found in a public place directly into a work computer?

options.text: There is no risk at all
It could contain malware designed to infect the system (a baiting attack)
It will automatically improve the computer's performance
It will only affect the USB drive itself
